episode_row: live-forward resolver stalled on a suspended/resumed game (CRITICAL)

commits.subject: fix(experiment): void suspended-resumed games in the live-forward resolver
commits.body:
A pick whose game was suspended and resumed the next day stalled the resolver
forever: the resumed game keeps its original officialDate, so its PA rows stay
filed under the earlier date while the slate dates the pick on the resume day,
and the (date, game_pk) join never matches -> permanent pending_outcomes. Per
BTS rules the resumed portion is never evaluated, so the pick is a terminal void.

Classify a still-missing row whose game_pk has PA but NONE on that row's own slate
date as a distinct void_suspended_resume status (a row-local check, so a multi-date
resolve pass stays correct); the date then resolves (resolved_with_voids) instead of
stalling, and future occurrences self-heal. A game with slate-date PA (the batter
just didn't play, even alongside stray off-date rows) stays pending, as does a game
absent from PA entirely; a malformed/null game_pk is coerced defensively (left
pending) rather than crashing the resolve.

Fixes the 2026-06-17 live_forward_resolution CRITICAL stall (game 824912 resumed
from 06-16). See docs/audit/2026-06-29-skip-threshold-and-discrimination.md.

commits.subject: fix(model): stop offering resume-date suspended games as candidates
commits.body:
A suspended game resumed on a later day still appears on that day's MLB schedule
with its original (earlier) officialDate. Per BTS rules the resumed portion is
never evaluated, so a pick on the resume day can never score -- the slate must not
offer it. _fetch_game_slots now skips schedule games whose officialDate is earlier
than the queried date (logging a count). The predicate lives in bts.picks
(lightgbm-free) so it is covered even without the model extra. The resolver void in
the sibling commit is the backstop; this stops them at the source.
